title: Book Two · Chapter 69: Ten Candles on Paper
story:
Warm spring turns into early summer. Ronan's birthday comes on a Sunday. Today he is ten.

Mum sets down the bowl at breakfast. Long, warm noodles fill it. Dad puts a small folded paper beside Ronan's spoon.

“Open it before the noodles get cold,” he says.

Ronan opens the paper. Ten candles stand above a very strange cake. The cake leans to one side.

“Did it fall?” Ronan asks.

“Only a little,” Dad says.

Mum looks over his shoulder. “The plate is too small.”

Ronan counts the candles. There are ten, with one dark dot above each. The dots are the flames. But they look like tiny insects.

“Can I blow them out?”

“Try.”

Ronan blows. The paper moves across the table. It slides toward Dad's bowl. Dad catches it.

“A strong birthday wind.”

After breakfast, Ronan gets a new exercise book and two pencils. The book is his own. It is not for a customer or a class task. He can choose the first page.

He hopes for another reading morning too. Nobody mentions one. He touches the smooth cover and puts the pencils beside it.

“Thank you,” he says.

Mum brushes his hair back with her hand. “Ten.”

“Still shorter than me,” Dad says.

“For now.”

In the afternoon, Jun and Leo come for a game. Mum gives them each a little sweet bun. They sit in the yard before they play. Jun breaks his bun and looks inside.

“Mine is empty.”

“That is the air part,” Leo says.

Ronan laughs with his mouth full. Mum tells him to swallow first. He tries to answer and nod at once. Everyone laughs again.

They play until the wall is in shade. Ronan loses the first game and wins the second. Jun leaves before the last round because his family is waiting.

That evening, Ronan opens the new exercise book. He draws the blue bike on the first page. The wheels are different sizes. He changes one wheel carefully. Then he adds the old bell.

On the next page, he writes ten at the top. He wants to draw something important below it. For a while, the page stays blank.

Then Dad calls him to help carry supper bowls. Ronan leaves the book open. When he returns later, he draws three bowls under the word. One is smaller than the others. He leaves space beside them for another drawing tomorrow.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

birthday＝生日；candle＝蜡烛；bowl＝碗。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan的十岁生日有哪些普通快乐？
2. 他没有得到什么，又实际得到了什么？

## 读句子

**He / draws / the blue bike on the first page.** 他／在第一页／画出蓝色自行车。
